title: Rupee hits 7-month high on FPI inflows, softer oil prices - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Over the past two trading days, the rupee has strengthened by nearly 72 paise

The rupee appreciated to a seven-month high of 93.5 against the US dollar, supported by improving market sentiment amid falling crude oil prices and oil marketing companies (OMCs) accessing the Reserve Bank of India’s special dollar window. The domestic currency gained 42.5 paise on the day, marking its second consecutive session of appreciation. Over the past two trading days, the rupee has strengthened by nearly 72 paise. The currency was last at these levels on April 17, when it traded around 92.6 per dollar.

Market participants attributed the rally to softer crude oil prices, renewed foreign portfolio investor (FPI) interest in Indian assets, and reduced dollar demand in the interbank market as OMCs increasingly sourced dollars directly from the RBI.

“State-run oil refiners such as IOC, BPCL and HPCL collectively buy about $8-10 billion every month. That demand has been largely removed from the interbank market because they are purchasing dollars directly from the RBI,” said Ritesh Bhansali, Deputy Chief Executive Officer at Mecklai Financial Services. He added that RBI restrictions on importers have also helped absorb liquidity from the market.

The RBI had earlier introduced measures to stabilise the rupee amid concerns that escalating geopolitical tensions and rising crude oil prices could push the currency towards the 100/dollar mark. One such measure allowed oil marketing companies to purchase dollars directly from the central bank, thereby reducing volatility in the foreign exchange market.

With the rupee now comfortably below the 94/dollar level, the RBI may eventually encourage OMCs to return to the open market for their dollar requirements, according to Anindya Banerjee, Commodity and Currency Analyst at Kotak Neo.

Meanwhile, crude oil prices have moderated, with Brent crude futures trading at around $93.7 a barrel. The stabilisation of currency markets has also coincided with a return of FPI inflows in November, providing additional support to the rupee against the greenback.

Meanwhile, analysts expect the rupee to appreciate further. “The rupee was significantly undervalued, so it needed a trigger. I think that’s what we have got,” Banerjee said, adding that the currency could appreciate to as much as 91.5/dollar without requiring RBI intervention.

Bhansali expects the rupee to strengthen further and forecasts it could reach 92.5 against the dollar over the next two months.
